sense: in questions, conditions and after a negative

terms.gloss: any (after a negative, and in questions that expect “no”)
evidence: Verg. G. 2.420: nōn ūlla est oleīs cultūra
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: ūllus stands in denials where an affirmation has aliquī, as quisquam does for aliquis (see anyone, anything). So after nōn, nec, sine and vix. “Not any” is nūllus (see no).

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.7: num quod officium aliud aliō majus sit (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 1.48: sī quī graviōre vulnere acceptō equō dēciderat (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: After sī, nisi, num and nē the ali- of aliquī drops, as in sī quis, sī quid (see someone, something).

terms.gloss: any at all, any you like
evidence: Ter. Ad. 254: ab quīvīs homine … beneficium accipere gaudeās (Lewis & Short, Ad. 2.3.1)
terms.comment: Any whatever, no matter which; also quīlibet (see anyone, anything, in the sense “no matter who, what”).

phrases.latin: Hispānī sine ūllā mōle in utrēs vestīmentīs conjectīs ipsī caetrīs superpositīs incubantēs flūmen trānāvēre
phrases.english: the Spaniards, without any fuss, put their clothes in leather bags, lay on their shields on top of them and swam the river

phrases.latin: contrā nōn ūlla est oleīs cultūra
phrases.english: olives, on the other hand, need no tending of any kind

phrases.latin: quod amant locum pūrum neque ipsī ūllum, ubi fuērunt, relincunt pūrum
phrases.english: because they love a clean place, and yet themselves leave no place clean where they have been

phrases.latin: ex quō togam virīlem sūmpsit nūllō diē prius ūllam pūblicam prīvātamque rem ēgit quam in Capitōlium īret
phrases.english: from the day he took the toga of manhood, he did no business of any kind, public or private, before going up to the Capitol

phrases.latin: quaeritur, num quod officium aliud aliō majus sit
phrases.english: the question is whether any duty is greater than another
